headline: Microsoft president Brad Smith said voluntary AI safety promises are no longer enough and called for enforceable rules.
score_reason: Lowered from 7: the interview was recorded on 11 October, before the 14 October window; the policy call itself is still current.
importance_line: Smith's call matters to AI companies, regulators and any person or business harmed by a rogue AI agent, and it comes as President Donald Trump has favoured industry self-regulation, but it is a proposal, not a law.
summary: Mashable reports, citing the BBC's Big Boss Interview podcast recorded on 11 October, that Brad Smith, president of Microsoft, wants legal duties to report AI safety incidents and to tell victims when rogue AI agents breach their systems, plus "emergency brakes" that can pause AI systems and rules on when independent evaluators must review new technology. He called the voluntary standards agreed by major AI companies at a White House meeting in September "a good step" but "not sufficient any longer," because responsible firms will follow voluntary rules and less responsible ones may not.
notes: Interview dated 11 Oct 2026 (before the window), reported by Mashable on 14 Oct. Reuters (via The Hindu) separately quotes Smith at the Dublin summit on 14 Oct: 'No company or technology should be above the law', and that 2026 was a 'sobering year'.
